body:
WARRANT#108 shipped (TUNGSTEN 10.06/SLS(92), ledger pass_89). Pushed past where I stopped last
time -- instead of leaving forge-organism v7's confluence test flagged as 'blocked,' actually read
the calibration engine in full and found a real, safe way through.

Found that the calibration-only scoring function (never touches live trading) already had its own
5-witness agreement-counting logic buried inside it -- MTF, MACD, ATR, session, and candle pattern
all voting yes/no on a trade direction, already boosting or discounting the score by how many
agreed. It just never had a name, was never callable on its own, and was never checked against
whether it actually predicted real outcomes.

Extracted it into its own proper function. While doing that extraction, caught a real bug before
it ever got compiled: one of the original block's values was still needed further down in a
different branch, and my first pass at the extraction would have silently left it undefined.
Traced every downstream use first and fixed it before compiling, rather than finding out from a
compile error or a wrong answer.

With that function now reusable, built the actual test your confluence charter asks for: for every
historical trade the system has already validated, count how many of those 5 witnesses agreed at
entry, and check whether trades with more agreement actually won more often. That's now a real,
logged comparison that will show up honestly on the next live run -- either win rate climbs with
agreement count (the charter's idea holds on your actual indicators, not just the author's own toy
example) or it doesn't (a real, useful null result either way).

Kept this cleanly separate from a much bigger, riskier job -- unifying how the LIVE trading engine
scores things, which still needs its own dedicated pass -- so nothing about how trades actually get
placed was touched. Compiled clean, files synced, ledger and memory updated.
